findings.claim: A leftover part whose title was edited can be missed if the edit has aged out of memory_versions. In that case the part stays active after a shorter re-save.
evidence: The only evidence for a renamed part is a memory_versions row whose title ends in '(part i/...)'. update() keeps only the last MaxVersions=5 rows (save.go:31, 389).
Each mem_update or body edit adds a row. About five later edits after the rename push the original '(part i/N)' row out.
Before this commit, a derived-key part was archived regardless of its title when no moved key matched, so this orphan case is new for the derived-key path.
Impact is low: it needs a rename plus more than 4 later edits, and it leaves one stale part active, not data loss.

findings.claim: The new tests do not cover a version-history match on a moved key with an unedited current title, or two leftover parts at once mixing derived and moved keys.
evidence: TestResavingASplitDocumentSparesAMemoryThatTookAnArchivedPartsKey checks only an unrelated active holder at the derived key.
The renamed-moved-part test checks archival through version history with only one leftover part (design/part-2).
No test uses oldParts >= 3 with a shorter re-save that mixes derived and moved keys.
Read internal/memory/save.go lines 100-230 and 365-400 (Save, splitInput, partKey, update).
SQL placeholders: 10 '?' and 10 bound arguments, matching.
The first LIKE is '% (part i/oldParts)', the second '% (part i/%)'; both match the intent.
The moved-key filter accepts only an all-digit suffix.
memories.id inside the correlated EXISTS subquery of an UPDATE is valid SQLite.
The status='active' filter keeps archived or superseded rows untouched.
